hook.text: A bezel swaps claws for a rim.

lines.text: A bezel swaps claws for a rim.
A bezel is a thin metal rim that wraps the stone's edge.
Full bezels wrap the stone, and half bezels leave two sides open.
Bezels are among the most secure settings, with nothing to snag.
That is why bezels suit soft stones like opal.
A setter solders the rim on and cuts a seat inside.
Then the edge is pushed over the stone and burnished smooth.
A bezel lets in slightly less light than prongs do.
In 3D, keep the rim wall at least half a millimeter thick.
lines.say: In three D, keep the rim wall at least half a millimeter thick.

lines.text: So a bezel holds the stone with a rim instead of claws.
A render shows the rim around the stone before anything is cast.

post.caption: A bezel setting holds a stone with a thin rim of metal instead of claws. Full bezels wrap the whole stone and half bezels leave two sides open, and bezels are among the most secure settings, which is why they suit soft stones like opal. A bezel lets in slightly less light than prongs, and in 3D the rim wall should be at least half a millimeter thick. The renders in this video were made with HeyGema.
